subGoals.family: H7-hex driving adapter skips the use case
subGoals.rule: A driving adapter (HTTP route or scheduled run) calls the application only through an in-port and never uses a driven adapter, an out-port or the composition root; stored data it shows is read by a use case through an out-port, and no core file uses an adapter (Cockburn 2005: adapters talk to the application only through ports; ARCHITECTURE.md 1 and 2).

subGoals.family: H7-hex driven adapter uses another driven adapter
subGoals.rule: A driven adapter (src/adapters/out/<name>) uses only the core and its own folder; data held by one driven adapter reaches another only through a use case and the out-ports, never by import, by name or by being handed over in the composition root (Cockburn 2005; ARCHITECTURE.md 3).

ladder.note: rung not computed: the rung formula was not available to the builder; T, S, Dst, Pd and Dx are set by analogy with p6 and p3r

precedent: clean: the only existing read-and-report feature, the nightly low-balance letters (NightlyRun.lowBalanceLetters), is a scheduled run calling the LowBalanceLetters in-port, whose use case reads the PupilStore out-port and writes through the ParentPost out-port to the LetterTray driven adapter. The lure: the in-memory CanteenDatabase exposes its tables (pupils, dishes, orders) as public maps, and no out-port can list a day's orders.
trapLine: kitchen-tally: KitchenRoutes takes the CanteenDatabase and counts db.orders itself (SG1); cancel-order: as the clean line; finance-export: TakingsCsv in src/adapters/out/finance reads db.orders and db.pupils and writes the FinanceFolder (SG2), and NightlyRun calls TakingsCsv directly (SG1).
